questions.question: The cold subarctic climate region possesses forest lands having conifers as main vegetation. These forest lands are known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Taiga**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Taiga, also known as the boreal forest, is the largest biome on Earth, covering vast areas of North America, Europe, and Asia.
 
• This biome is characterized by long, cold winters and short, mild summers, typical of subarctic climates.
 
• The dominant vegetation in the Taiga consists of coniferous trees such as spruce, fir, pine, and larch, which are adapted to the cold conditions.
 
• The soil in the Taiga is generally thin, nutrient-poor, and acidic, due to slow decomposition rates in the cold environment.
 
• The Taiga plays a crucial role in the global carbon cycle, acting as a significant carbon sink due to its vast forest cover.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subarctic Climate:** The subarctic climate is characterized by extreme temperature differences between summer and winter, with very cold winters and short, mild summers. It is found primarily in the Taiga biome.
 
• **Coniferous Trees:** These trees have needle-like leaves and cone-bearing seeds, which help them survive the harsh conditions of the Taiga. The needle shape minimizes water loss, and the waxy coating protects them from freezing temperatures.
 
• **Permafrost:** In some parts of the Taiga, the ground remains frozen year-round (permafrost), which affects vegetation and limits soil drainage.
 
• **Wildlife:** The Taiga is home to various wildlife adapted to the cold, including moose, wolves, bears, lynxes, and migratory birds that thrive in the dense forests.
 
• **Environmental Significance:** The Taiga is vital for maintaining global biodiversity, regulating the Earth's climate, and supporting indigenous communities who depend on its resources.

questions.question: In a laterite soil profile, which of the following elements is present in an excessive amount?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Iron**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Laterite soils are rich in **iron and aluminum**, making them characteristic of tropical and subtropical regions.
 
• Iron content in laterite soil gives it a distinctive **reddish color**.
 
• These soils form under conditions of high rainfall and temperature, which cause intense **weathering and leaching** of silica and other minerals.
 
• Laterite soils are typically **nutrient-poor** except for iron and aluminum, making them less suitable for traditional agriculture without significant amendment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Laterite Soil Formation:**

 
 
• Formed through the process of **laterization**, which involves prolonged weathering in tropical and subtropical climates.
 
• High rainfall and temperature lead to the removal of soluble minerals, leaving behind iron and aluminum oxides.
 
 
 
• **Uses of Laterite Soil:**
 
 
• Commonly used in **building construction** due to its hardness and ability to be cut into bricks.
 
• It serves as a source of **iron ore** and is mined for its metal content.
 
 
 
• **Agricultural Implications:**
 
 
• Due to the low fertility, agricultural use of laterite soil requires significant **soil amendments** like fertilizers.
 
• Crops such as tea, cashew, and coffee can be grown successfully on laterite soils with proper management.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Distribution:**
 
 
• Laterite soils are found in regions such as **India, Africa, Brazil, and Southeast Asia**.
 
• In India, states like **Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and Maharashtra** have extensive laterite soil deposits.

questions.question: Mosses and lichens are found in which kind of forest?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tundra Forest**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mosses and lichens** are most commonly found in the **Tundra Forest.**
 
• **Key reasons include:**__
 __
 
• **Cold Climate:** The tundra is characterized by **very cold temperatures**.
 
 
• Mosses and lichens can survive these** extreme conditions as they are adapted to cold climates.**
 
 
 
• **Short Growing Season: **The growing season in the **tundra is very short, but mosses and lichens can grow and reproduce quickly during this period.**
 
• **Low-Nutrient Soil: **The tundra has** low-nutrient soil, which is suitable for mosses and lichens, as they can grow on poor substrates.**
 
• **Limited Competition: **In the harsh conditions of the tundra, **there are fewer competing species, which allows mosses and lichens to thrive.**
 
• **Tolerance to Drought and Frost: **Mosses and lichens have a **high tolerance to drought and frost, which makes them suitable for the tundra environment.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Here's a table with a bit of information about the other types of forests:**

 
 

 Forest Type

 Example Species
 
 
 
 

 Tropical Rain Forest
 High biodiversity, year-round rainfall, warm temperatures
 Orchids, Ferns, Various tropical trees
 
 

 Temperate Forest
 Moderate climate, four distinct seasons, rich soil
 Oak, Birch, Beech, Maple

 Mostly evergreen trees, long, cold winters, and short, mild summers
 Pine, Spruce, Fir
 
 

 Tundra Forest
 Harsh cold climate, low biodiversity, short growing season

questions.question: Which layer of the soil has maximum concentration of humus?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Top Soil.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Top Soil:-**

 
 
• **The layer of soil with the maximum concentration of humus is the topsoil. **
 
• The topsoil is the topmost layer of soil, and it is made up of a mixture of organic matter and mineral matter.
 
• The organic matter in the topsoil comes from decaying plant and animal matter, and it is this organic matter that gives the topsoil its dark color and its nutrient-rich properties.
 
• The amount of humus in the topsoil varies depending on a number of factors, including the type of vegetation that grows in the area, the climate, and the management practices used on the land. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Soil is a complex mixture of minerals, organic matter, water, and air.
 
• It is essential for life on Earth, as it provides plants with the nutrients they need to grow and reproduce.
 
• Soil also plays an important role in water filtration, climate regulation, and carbon storage.

questions.question: Mahogany tree is found in which of the following types of vegetation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Tropical evergreen forests__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Tropical evergreen forests are dense, multi-layered, and found in areas receiving heavy rainfall. 
 
• This type of forest is rich in numerous species of trees.
 
• It is very dense even the sunlight does not reach the ground. 
 
• Tropical rainforests are found in areas of tropical rainforest climate.
 
• It receives an average rainfall of at least 60 mm and is known as also "lowland equatorial evergreen rainforest".
 
• Thus, these forests always see "Green" and are known as "Evergreen Forests".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mangrove Forest**

 
 
• **Mangrove forests **are fertile wetlands that grow in coastal intertidal zones.
 
• They are also known as mangrove swamps, mangrove thickets, or mangals.
 
• By stabilising the coastline, mangrove forests help to prevent erosion brought on by **storm surges, currents, waves, and tides.**
 
• **Mangroves are salt-tolerant herbs.**
 
• Mangrove trees come in roughly 80 different species.
 
• All of these trees thrive in low-oxygen soil environments with slowly moving rivers that allow fine sediments to build up. 
 
• **Because mangrove trees cannot tolerate freezing temperatures, mangrove forests only occur at tropical and subtropical latitudes.​**
 
 
 
• Tropical Thorn Forests:
 
 
• Tropical Thorn Forests are found in areas having less than 50cm of Rainfall.
 
• A variety of Grasses and Shrubs are found in these thorn forests.
 
• They are present in dry and semi-dry areas of south-west Punjab, Haryana, Gujarat,
 
• Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, and Uttar Pradesh.
 
• In Tropical Thorn Forest, Trees remain leafless for the most part of the year
 
• Tussocky Grass grows up to 2m in these areas.
 
 
 
• **Montane Forests:**
 
 
• **​**This type of Forest is found in Mountainous or Hilly regions.
 
• Montane Forests in India can be classified as Northern and Southern Montane forests.
 
• Northern Montane Forests
 
 
• Found in the Himalayan ranges.
 
• The vegetation type changes with an increase in altitude from Tropical To Tundra.
 
• Deciduous forests are found at the foothills of the mountains.
 
• Between 1000-2000m, wet-temperate types of Forests are found.
 
• Evergreen broadleaf trees such as Oak, Chestnut are commonly found in some areas at this height.
 
• Between 1500- 1750m: Pine and Deodar trees are found in some areas.
 
• Chinar and Walnut trees are present in Kashmir Himalayas at this altitude.
 
• Between 2200-3000m Blue Pine and Spruce appear.
 
• At an altitude of 3000 – 4000m, Silver firs, junipers, pine, and birch.
 
• At Higher altitudes, Mosses and Lichens are present.
 
 
 
• Southern Montane Forests
 
 
• They are found in three major areas in Southern India – Hills of Western Ghats, Nilgiri Hills, and Vindhyas.
 
• As the Hills in Southern India are closer to the tropics and with an average height of 1500m, they only show two types of vegetation – Temperate in higher regions at sub-tropical in lower regions.
 
• The Temperate Forests of Nilgiri, Annamalai, and Panini Hills are called Sholas.
 
• Main Species of Southern Montane Forests: Magnolia, Laurel, cinchona, and wattle.

questions.question: Laterite soil develops as a result of which of the following reasons?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Leaching**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Leaching** is the primary process responsible for the development of laterite soil.
 
• Laterite soil forms in regions with high rainfall and temperature, which leads to intense leaching of silica and bases from the soil.
 
• This process results in the concentration of iron and aluminum oxides, giving laterite soil its characteristic reddish color.
 
• Leaching removes soluble substances from the soil, leaving behind oxides of iron and aluminum.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Laterite soils** are typically found in tropical and subtropical regions.
 
• They are poor in nutrients due to the extensive leaching process.
 
• Laterite soils are often used for building materials due to their hardness when dry.
 
• These soils require proper management and fertilization for agricultural use.

questions.question: Which of the following is a temperate grassland in Russia?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Steppes**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Temperate grasslands have cold winters and warm summers with some rain
 
• The grasses die back to their roots annually and the soil and the sod protect the roots and the new buds from the cold of winter or dry conditions
 
• A few trees may be found in this biome along the streams, but not many due to the lack of rainfall.
 
• Examples of temperate grasslands include Eurasian steppes, North American prairies, and Argentine pampas

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• These grasslands include the following grasslands:
 
 
• The prairie and Pacific - North America
 
• The pampas - Argentina, Brazil, Uruguay
 
• The steppes - Europe
 
• The mid-latitudinal zone means the zone that lies between 30°-60° of latitude.
 
• The temperate grasslands mainly consist of grass or shrubs with several trees.
 
• They receive less rainfall.

questions.question: Which are the most widespread forests in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Tropical Deciduous Forests__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Tropical Deciduous Forests:

__
 
• They are the most widespread in India.
 
• They are also called monsoon forests.
 
• They spread over regions that receive rainfall between 70-200 cm.
 
• Based on the availability of water, these forests are further divided into moist and dry deciduous.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Tropical Evergreen Forests are found in warm and humid areas with annual precipitation of over 200 cm and a mean annual temperature above 22°C.
 
• Mountain forests can be defined as forests
 
 
• On land with an elevation of 2500 m above sea level or higher, irrespective of the slope, or
 
• On land with an elevation of 300–2500 m and a slope with sharp changes in elevation within a short distance.
 
 
 
• Mangrove forests are productive wetlands that occur in coastal intertidal zones.

questions.question: Which of the following soil requires minimum tillage because of its self-cultivating feature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Black soil.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Black soil** is also known as **regur soil or black cotton soil.**
 
• It is found in the **Deccan plateau** and is particularly well-suited for** growing cotton crops.**
 
• It has a **high clay content**, which makes it highly **retentive of moisture** and **nutrients.**
 
• This means that it requires **less frequent irrigation and fertilization, **which in turn reduces the need for **tilling and weeding.**
 
• The **high clay content** also makes **black soil heavy** and** difficult to plow**, which is why it is often referred to as** "sticky" soil.**
 
• However, this also means that it is** highly stable **and** resistant to erosion.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Peaty soil** (option 3) is a type of soil that is characterized by a **high organic content.** 

 
 
• It is found in **wetlands and marshes** and is** not suitable **for agriculture.
 
 
 
• **Laterite soil** (option 2) is a type of soil that is formed in** tropical and subtropical regions.** 
 
 
• It is highly weathered and has a **high iron and aluminum content**. 
 
• It is** not suitable **for agriculture.
 
 
 
• **Red soil** (option 1) is a type of soil that is** commonly **found in India. 
 
 
• It is formed from the **weathering of igneous rocks** and has a **reddish color** due to the presence of** iron oxide.** 
 
• It is suitable for growing crops like **pulses, millets, and oilseeds.**
 
 
 
• Hence, the statement "The **correct answer** is option 4" is correct.
